verdict.rationale: Poke's docs describe a browsable directory at poke.com/recipes that lists first-party and approved third-party recipes, including prebuilt ones for services like Linear and Webflow. Users connect these integrations to Poke and can manage them (disconnect, refresh), and can add any MCP-compatible server directly if a service isn't listed. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the directory and add flow, and detailed documentation of the directory's breadth and step-by-step install UX.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can browse a directory of third-party apps and connectors and add them to the assistant

citations.quote: Go to poke.com/recipes to browse all first-party and approved third-party recipes.
Integrations let you connect your favorite apps and services to Poke.
You'll find prebuilt recipes for popular services: Linear - Automate issue and project management
All new and existing users can use Poke Recipes to easily set up automations and integrations, as well as share their set-ups with others.
If the service you want isn't available as a Recipe, you can connect any MCP-compatible server directly
